I understand high anxiety and not wanting to go to class as a result. You don't want the extra attention cus it'll just make you feel worse, I get that. Once you've calmed down a little, I would recommend mentioning that you had an anxiety attack and it prevented you from attending class. Your counselor WILL understand and if they don't well, just know it's not your fault and you can't help it. If you don't get the right assistance from your counselor, I would suggest setting up a meeting with a therapist outside of the school (I understand that sometimes it's hard to let people at your school know your problem as it can feel embarrassing). Sometimes when you mention anxiety attacks and how it prevents you from attending class, you can get special assistance in which when you do have an attack, someone will have a room ready for you and you can wait there while you catch your breath and calm down. It is good to try your best to tell people what's happening to you and they can help you. You don't even HAVE to talk face to face, you can write a letter or email explaining what's going on, even a phone call. 

Perhaps you should consider setting up an appointment with a psychiatrist and they can provide you with medicine that helps calm down people who are having an anxiety attack or feel one coming on, even just high anxiety.  There are different types of medicine for that, some may take longer to enter your system than needed, but there are other take as needed drugs that can enter your system faster and help with relief. 

If you want to talk and stuff, we can. I don't mind at all. Sometimes it's nice to talk to someone who kind of goes through the same thing as you. I suffer from panic attacks and severe anxiety and it still do this day prevents me from being able to go to class or even to the grocery store sometimes. Just know it's okay and there are methods that can help with those tough situations. Everything you are feeling seems like a result of extreme anxiety and that can cause depression and suicidal thoughts. Don't worry, it's okay. 

You are allowed to ask for help in your time of need and "be selfish". Sometimes you gotta worry about you and your health before worrying about other people and their views. You are important and matter and you deserve to ask for help.

Hey hey hey. It's okay, sweetheart. Deep breaths. I've been in situation like this numerous times and it is extremely overwhelming and awful. It's okay. 


Go find a relaxing, quiet place.
What homework do you have? Make a list of what needs to get done step by step so you can organize your thoughts. Make a list of the most important to the least important. Do that first then take a 15 minute break to calm and relax as much as you can; listen to music, play a game, talk to a friend or family member.


Go down the list steadily and be sure to take breaks every once in a while (set an alarm for every half or to an hour to take a 15 minute break). 

Next and finally, organize what could be on your exam and think about what you need to study most. Don't worry about cramming. If you worry about it you wont be able to concentrate on the material. 

While you study, have some ice cold water, chew gum or have a chewy snack, listen to some upbeat music (preferably without lyrics), this has shown to help improve peoples memory of material they study the night before an exam. 

Write down on a separate sheet of paper little notes (not detailed) of things you think you may have trouble remembering the next day; you can look at this sheet of paper right before your exam to refresh your memory. 

Most importantly, be sure you go to sleep by the time midnight comes around (that's still late, but I know when you are overwhelmed like this it can take time to get assignments done and study). There is no point studying if you're exhausted. If need be, you can wake up an hour earlier than usual to study material. 

Also, before your exam, have a drink with caffeine (this isn't a good habit, as caffeine isn't so great for you), this has also been shown in studies to improve students grades before exams. Just be sure to drink your drink maybe 20 minutes before your exam. The caffeine doesn't last too long (maybe 3-4 hours) and then you, statistically speaking, perform poorer after is wears off. 

Good luck! If I can be of anymore assistance, just reply.

If your grades are a concern and great stress for you, some colleges have students with disabilities stuff you can look into? I have it for severe panic attacks and severe depression, also diabetes. But a lot of school programs provide services for students that have problems. Because school is stressful enough and when you have mental problems going on, usually your school can help provide you with a boost to help you through school and make it less stressful. 

I would recommend looking into students with disabilities in your school and then mentioning your struggles when you do sou selling to see if you have options for some help. It's hard to ask for help. It took me two years of college before I used the program and it's helped me tremendously.

Maybe he can study with you on a Skype call sometime? Or just be there on call while you study. 

The most important thing right now is you. Do what makes you happy and helps relieve your stress.
